comparison: Both evaluate the monochromatic ERG data showing wavelength-specific defects (C6, C7, C53-C55, C65-C70, C124-C125). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with strong statistical backing and internal consistency. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, questioning whether single mutants affect UV detection given no significant UV/blue changes, and noting the ERG may lack resolution to detect differences or that blue light may overwhelm UV effects.

Both evaluate immunohistochemistry data on EAAT5b/EAAT7 spatial distribution (C9, C10, C56, C77-C85, C97, C129-C131). Both rate this SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative intensity measurements and correlation analysis with adequate sample size (n=11). Peer reviewers confirm solid evidence for localization patterns with no concerns raised about the anatomical findings themselves.

Both evaluate EAAT5b hunting behavior data (C58, C99-C104, C136). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting appropriate statistical tests show no significant differences and conclusions are appropriately cautious. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, emphasizing the surprising contradiction with predicted role and noting lack of intensity-specific comparisons limits interpretation of the null result.

Both evaluate EAAT7 enhanced hunting behavior (C59, C60, C105-C113, C137). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting consistent enhancement across metrics with robust pooled statistics and appropriate interpretation of paradoxical enhancement. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, critically noting the lack of intensity-specific comparisons prevents concluding whether EAAT7 KO allows detection of weaker stimuli.

Both evaluate OMR data for EAAT5b (C61, C116). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting statistical evidence for eaat5b defect (p=0.01) and appropriate interpretation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting only one stimulus was tested, making it unclear whether the defect reflects sensitivity, resolution, or other factors.

OpenEval R5 and Peer R6 both address EAAT7 OMR results (C117). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting absence of eaat7 defect and appropriate acknowledgment of ERG-behavior dissociation. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, confirming the observation that OMR was not reduced in EAAT7 mutants, though noting it contradicts predictions.

Both evaluate the integrative conclusion about EAAT roles in chromatic processing (C8, C12-C14, C63-C64, C89, C126, C150). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting the conclusion is well-supported by combined ERG, anatomical, and behavioral data. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with mixed views: acknowledging solid evidence and appropriately conservative conclusions, but noting contradictions with predictions and that conclusions are necessarily vague due to data resolution limitations.

Both evaluate mGluR6b distribution data (C86). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to N=1 sample being insufficient for firm conclusions. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, explicitly recommending either adding more samples or removing the data as it is based on a single fish and does not significantly impact main conclusions.

OpenEval R7 evaluates hunting assay validation data (C92-C96, C134-C135) and rates it SUPPORTED, noting clear wavelength preference, intensity dependence, and habituation effects establish the assay as valid. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological validation claims.

OpenEval R9 evaluates acknowledgment of technical limitations in ERG UV-blue discrimination (C71, C127) and rates it SUPPORTED as an appropriately acknowledged caveat. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this technical limitation acknowledgment.

OpenEval R10 evaluates mechanistic speculation about kinetic differences and behavioral implications (C114-C115, C138-C144) and rates it UNCERTAIN, noting interpretations are speculative though plausible. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these mechanistic hypotheses.

OpenEval R11 evaluates speculation about OMR pathway compensation explaining ERG-behavior discrepancy (C119-C120, C145-C147) and rates it UNCERTAIN as untested hypothesis. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this compensation hypothesis, though peer reviewers note the contradictions generally.

OpenEval R12 evaluates acknowledgment of knowledge gap about EAAT expression outside retina (C148-C149) and rates it SUPPORTED as appropriate limitation of scope. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific knowledge gap acknowledgment.
